Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: POC plan recap + asked environment preference

Thanks for taking the time today, Daniel — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of ask
- Objective: 60-day evaluation to validate latency, cost per 1k tokens, and integration with Acme’s EHR anonymization pipeline.
- Primary success criteria: average 95th percentile latency < 120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), embedding recall >= 0.86 on our supplied test set, and no PHI leakage in the anonymization pass.

Environment options we discussed
1) Hosted sandbox (Redwood-hosted trial) — fastest to stand up, sample dataset, shared compute.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity) — isolated GPUs, predictable throughput; 1-week lead time to provision.
3) VPC/on‑prem pilot — required for full security review; needs network firewall rules and our deploy package.

Proposed next steps
- You to confirm which environment you prefer (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) and primary evaluation owner (Emma or Daniel).
- We’ll send SOW + trial configuration once environment is selected.
- Tentative timeline: kickoff week of 2/23 if hosted; dedicated/VPC may push to early March.

Attachments: draft SOW and network checklist attached for quick read.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Acme_POCTest_SOW.pdf (pdf, 2 pages), network_requirements.xlsx (xlsx, 1 sheet)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

Success criteria (internal)
- Latency: 95th <= 150ms acceptable initially, target 120ms.
- Accuracy: embedding recall >= 0.85 on our 500-query set.
- Security: service must sign Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and we need logs for data access during the trial.

Environment preference
- We want to start with the Redwood-hosted sandbox to move fast. If results look good we’ll request a Dedicated sandbox for a second phase.

Ownership and roles
- Primary contact for trial execution: Emma Hartman (emma.hartman@acmehealth.com).
- IT lead for firewall/network questions: Mark Lopez (mark.lopez@acmehealth.com). He may reach out for the network checklist.

Timing
- Hosted kickoff: please schedule kickoff call week of 2/23.

I’ve attached a short SOW redline; will confirm signatures internally once we see the final SOW from Redwood.

—Daniel

Subject: Re: POC plan and sandbox access for Acme Health - hosted vs dedicated details

Hi Daniel / Emma — Vivek here, sales engineer on this engagement. Thanks for choosing hosted to start, that’s the fastest path. A few notes to make the trial effective and avoid surprises: 

Hosted sandbox details (summary)
- Provisioning: we can stand up a tenant and invite your team within 2 business days after SOW + trial account info.
- Data: recommend sending a 500-row anonymized sample (CSV) and the 500-query eval set. We’ll also run our internal regression tests.
- Observability: we will grant read-only Redwood Console access for route-level latency and cost. You will get token-level breakdowns for the trial tokens you generate.
- Security & compliance: hosted trials are run in a shared compute environment but we provide audit logs and can sign a limited-trial BAA addendum. Full VPC/on-prem is required for scope with PHI beyond anonymized test sets.

Dedicated sandbox considerations
- Stronger isolation and predictable throughput; typical lead time 7–10 days for capacity reservation.
- Better for throughput validation at scale (high concurrency).

VPC/on‑prem pilot
- Necessary if your security/compliance team disallows shared-hosted compute for any PHI workflows. This requires network allowlist, HSM/KMS details, and estimated 3–4 week setup.

Action items I’ll take once you confirm hosted:
- Provision hosted tenant and create evaluation project.
- Provide onboarding doc + sample CURL/SDK commands and an initial prompt library.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff (we suggest 2/24 or 2/25).

If you confirm dedicated later we’ll open a capacity request and share a performance runbook.

Vivek Kulkarni
